chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn [Qays], from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave girl shared between two men who both emancipated her together. Then one of the two permitted her private part to his partner. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for him. And whichever of the two dies before his companion, half of her becomes free from the side of the one who died, and half remains managed (as a slave).'

I said: 'What is your view if the remaining one of the two wants to touch her, is that for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless he decides her emancipation and marries her with her pleasure, similar to what he intends.' I said to him: 'Hasn't half of her become free? She has controlled half her neck, and the other half is for the remaining one of the two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'If she makes her master permissible regarding her private part and permits it to him, is that allowed for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not allowed for him.' I said: 'Why is it not allowed for her, just as you permitted the one who had half of her, when he permitted her private part to his partner from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the free woman does not gift her private part, nor lend it, nor permit it. But for her from herself is a day, and for the one who managed her is a day. If he wishes to marry her by Mut'ah with something during the day in which she controls herself, let him enjoy her with something, little or much.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave girl shared between two masters where one permits the other sexual access?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'partial emancipation' (tadbir), where a slave shared by two masters becomes half-free upon one's death, a concept rooted in the Prophetic tradition of manumission shares. It distinguishes between the master's right to sexual access and the woman's agency, noting that while she cannot unilaterally gift her body, the remaining master must contract a Mut'ah (temporary marriage) with her for the duration of her enslaved share, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual consent and contractual clarity in mixed-status unions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a slave girl between two men who both managed her together. Then one of the two permitted her sanctity to his partner. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is Permissible for him, and whichever of the two dies before his companion, so half of her would be free from the side of the one who dies, and half of her would be managed’.

I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if the remaining one of the two wants to touch her, would that be for him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, unless decided her emancipation, and he marries her with her pleasure from it, similar to what he intends’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Did not half of her become free, and she was in control of her emancipated half, and the other half being for the remaining one of the two?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

I said, ‘Supposing she were to make her master to be in permission from her private parts, would that be Permissible for her?’ Heasws said: ‘That is not allowed for him’. I said, ‘Why is that not allowed for her just as she allowed is for the one who had half of her for him, where she allowed her private part to his partner from it?’ Heasws said: ‘The free woman can neither gift her private part, not can she expose it, nor permit it, but for her from her half would be a day, and for the one who manages her would be a day. Iasws would love it if he would marry her by Mut’a with something during the day which she is in control of herself, so let him do Mut’a with her with something, be it little or more’.
